name: Title 1
text: Introduction

name: TextBox 5
text:
AI infrastructure teams must decide where workloads run, when to replan and how to recover from failure — often under cost, capacity and policy pressure.

Traditional observability shows utilization and alerts, but leaves the decision to the operator.

ARVA AI is a simulation-first autonomous decision-intelligence control plane. It observes a persistent GPU digital twin, forecasts demand, detects operational risk, compares plans, validates policy and records outcomes.

The central question: not only “What is happening now?” but “What should happen next — and why?”

name: Title 1
text: Literature Survey

name: TextBox 5
text:
Cluster management research shows that resource allocation is more than simple placement.

Borg demonstrated policy-aware cluster management at very large scale, combining admission control, packing, monitoring and simulation tools.

Tiresias focused on distributed deep-learning jobs, where uncertain duration, multi-GPU demand and queue delay make general schedulers insufficient.

Gavel showed why hardware heterogeneity matters: different models perform differently across accelerator types, so allocation policy must be heterogeneity-aware.

These works motivate ARVA AI’s combination of workload evidence, constrained placement and alternative-plan evaluation.

name: Title 1
text: Literature Survey

name: TextBox 5
text:
ARVA AI translates research lessons into an operator-facing decision loop.

A digital twin creates a safe, deterministic environment for forecasting demand, testing failures and evaluating recovery.

Instead of exposing a single opaque scheduling result, ARVA evaluates five heuristics plus an OR-Tools CP-SAT alternative under the same workload state.

Every candidate plan carries objective values, policy violations, rationale and expected outcome.

The design joins optimization quality with explainability, governance and replayable evidence.

name: Title 1
text: Research Gap

name: TextBox 3
text:
Operational gap: Existing infrastructure dashboards reveal utilization and incidents, but do not explain the best next action.

Optimization gap: A scheduler may generate a placement, yet operators need alternatives that expose trade-offs among cost, queue delay, SLA and energy.

Governance gap: Automated actions need explicit policy checks, approval gates, role-based access and an immutable audit trail.

Safety gap: Connecting experimental AI directly to production clusters creates operational risk.

ARVA AI addresses these gaps through a simulation-first, closed-loop control plane that keeps decisions measurable, explainable and governed.

name: Title 1
text: Project Objectives

name: TextBox 3
text:
1. Model a persistent, heterogeneous GPU fleet as a deterministic digital twin.

2. Produce demand forecasts and evidence-backed capacity, queue, cost and reliability risks.

3. Compare FIFO, priority, fair-share, bin-packing, deadline-aware and CP-SAT plans on a common state.

4. Enforce policy guardrails across simulation, recommendation, approval and controlled-autonomous modes.

5. Give operators a complete decision trail: alternatives, rationale, actor, execution state and measured outcome.

6. Demonstrate disruption recovery and repeatable scheduler evaluation.

name: Title 1
text: Problem Statement

name: TextBox 7
text: Decision intelligence for AI infrastructure

name: TextBox 9
text:
GPU infrastructure is heterogeneous, shared and disruption-prone. Demand spikes, deadline-sensitive jobs, rising prices and node failures can interact faster than manual workflows.

The challenge is to recommend a feasible action that balances throughput, urgency, cost, power and safety — while allowing an operator to understand and govern that choice.

ARVA AI addresses this challenge in a controlled simulator before real infrastructure adapters are introduced.

name: Title 1
text: Result and Analysis

name: TextBox 1
text:
Verification confirms that ARVA AI is a working, deterministic simulation-first MVP.

Validation gates
• Backend lint and 15 pytest tests passed
• Frontend lint, test suite, type check and production build passed
• Docker services, database migrations, authentication, security headers, WebSocket telemetry and durable Redis events passed
• Seeded environment: 3 clusters, 15 GPU nodes, 3 profiles, 3 teams and 200 workloads

Demonstrated scenario
A 90-minute baseline was followed by a demand spike, urgent deadline workload, 45% GPU price increase and active-node failure. The system produced forecasts, risks, alternative plans, policy checks and a repeatable recovery sequence.

name: Title 1
text:
Conclusion
ARVA AI combines a persistent GPU digital twin, forecasting, risk evidence, scheduler alternatives, CP-SAT placement and policy controls in one explainable loop.

Current boundary
The project is intentionally simulation-first: it does not yet write to Kubernetes or cloud control planes.

Future work
Add audited infrastructure adapters, TLS and secret rotation, managed PostgreSQL/Redis with backups, richer ML forecasting and production safety reviews.
